title: Object orientation: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and composition

videos.script: This course is about design. Not about a language, and not about a framework. {{title}} Design is the set of decisions about where code goes and what each piece is allowed to know. Those decisions outlive the syntax by decades. {{decades}} Before the patterns, the four ideas they are built from. Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and composition. {{four}} You will meet each one in a small program about a library. A loan that refuses to be returned twice. {{loan}} Books and films that share a parent. {{items}} Reminders that go out by e-mail, by text or on paper, through one call. {{channels}} And a member who switches from e-mail to text without becoming a different object. {{member}} First, though, your lab. Every program in this course runs, and you will run it on your own computer. It needs Python, a terminal and an editor, and nothing else. {{lab}} The programs are in Python whatever language you came here with. The next section says why, and how to read them in yours. {{language}}
